title: Rabbi Ashyan
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Yona’s student, as at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Terumot, chapter 1, where he speaks in Rabbi Yonah’s name, and likewise in Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 8:7 and Horayot, supplied locator ספ״מ: “Rabbi Ashyan, Rabbi Yonah,” etc. In Aggadat Bereshit, chapter 70, he speaks in Rabbi Chilkiyah’s name. He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 3:1 and Kohelet Rabbah 9:11. Hyman considers it very likely that he is the one sometimes called Rabbi Shiyan; see his entry.

notes.text: The supplied Horayot locator ספ״מ remains literal and unidentified; no chapter 40 or categorical end-of-book conversion is imposed. The possible name identification is Hyman’s. This locator question keeps the notice held.

The enlarged printed entry (Hyman, vol. I, p. 261) appears to read ספ״ב. The supplied ספ״מ is kept. Jerusalem Talmud Horayot 2:7:3, in the final halakhah of chapter 2, names Rabbi Ashyan, Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Bun bar Kahana in the objection about the High Priest. Seder HaDorot also identifies chapter 2. The consulted Kohelet Rabbah has the parallel funeral story at 9:10, where Ashyan speaks about speech and Rabbi Zeira about the eulogy. In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 3:1, Ashyan also states that the dead hear their eulogy like a dream. The Krakow Hebrew of Aggadat Bereshit 70 names Ashyan in Rabbi Chilkiyah’s name.
